question: On plain 4% up days (no burst filter), does a longer prior tight base (consol_days) grade the day? Expect longer consol_days = better stop-R (Minervini VCP / O'Neil flat-base logic: the longer the base, the bigger the eventual move).
plain: Minervini/O'Neil idea: a stock that spent a long time building a tight base before a 4% up day should perform better than one with no base at all.
